title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
excerpt: How little of a pretrained large language model (LLM) has to change for it to acquire new capabilities? We find that zeroing fewer than 0.05% of its weights, with no other modification, matches full fine-tuning (FFT) at scale across three LLM post-training regimes: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, supervised fine-tuning, and on-policy distillation. Our method, Deletion Tuning, learns a binary mask over the gate projection of transformer blocks. Two practical advantages follow: the trained mask is hundreds to thousands of times smaller than the corresponding FFT checkpoint, and Deletion Tuning forgets far less, which addresses a central challenge in continual learning. ai.summary: The paper presents Deletion Tuning, a method that zeroes less than 0.05% of an LLM's weights via a learned binary mask, achieving performance comparable to full fine‑tuning across RL, supervised, and distillation regimes.
ai.why: Offers a lightweight way to adapt LLMs with minimal parameter changes, reducing compute and storage overhead for developers.

title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
excerpt: As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense. However, existing benchmarks rely on annotators who rate each video with a single score based on intuition, yielding ratings that are subjective and do not tell which physical principle is violated. We introduce PhyRubric, a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework for evaluating physical commonsense in T2V generation. For each caption, PhyRubric constructs a caption-specific rubric before any video is seen, decomposing the caption into semantic and physical items, and derives scores from item-level verdicts grounded in timestamped…

ai.summary: PhyRubric is a diagnostic evaluation framework for text-to-video models that assesses physical commonsense using rubric-grounded criteria rather than single subjective scores. It identifies specific physical principles violated in generated videos to provide more granular feedback.
ai.why: Provides a more rigorous method for evaluating the physical plausibility of video generation models, useful for researchers benchmarking world-simulation capabilities.

title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
excerpt: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. This leaves unclear which capabilities they share, how their training objectives interact, and whether one model can perform all three well. We introduce the One Table Benchmark (), spanning 56 datasets, 46 registered methods, and 20 capability axes under aligned data splits and explicit task contracts. We compare task ranks on aligned support, train five backbones under all seven non-empty objective combinations on five datasets with three seeds, and contrast fixed-model profiles with specialist portfolios. Rank comparisons connect imputation and prediction…

ai.summary: The authors release the One Table Benchmark, covering 56 tabular datasets, 46 methods, and 20 capability axes to evaluate models on generation, imputation, and prediction tasks using aligned splits and task contracts.
ai.why: Provides a unified way to compare generalist tabular models, helping developers choose or train versatile models for data‑centric AI.

title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
excerpt: Discrete autoregressive modeling, notably through next-token prediction, has become a cornerstone of modern language models. Extending this paradigm to vision allows visual and language models to converge on a unified framework, thereby fostering shared methodology and infrastructure. This work investigates a central question: how far can a finite discrete vocabulary go in representing the richness of the visual world? We present dNaViT, a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that produces discrete visual primitives analogous to language tokens. Built upon a frozen pretrained encoder, dNaViT applies lightweight residual modulation with a dual-branch objective to inject…

ai.summary: The paper dNaViT proposes a Discrete Native‑resolution Vision Transformer that uses a finite discrete vocabulary to represent visual data, achieving competitive performance on standard vision benchmarks.
ai.why: Offers a new approach to unify vision and language modeling that could inspire open‑source vision model implementations.

title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
excerpt: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define…

ai.summary: ProTEUS is a world model trained on deep mutational scanning data that predicts the effects of individual protein mutations to guide closed-loop protein evolution in silico.

title: Embodied First Exam
excerpt: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. We hope it serves as a first exam for coding agents before they enter the physical world, with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites that go…

ai.summary: The paper introduces the Embodied First Exam, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents' ability to control robots, allowing agents to choose their own control approach (direct or code-based) rather than relying on fixed visuomotor policies.
ai.why: Provides a new evaluation framework for developers working on agentic robotics, testing the viability of using LLMs/coding agents for physical-world control.

title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
excerpt: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a…

ai.summary: The paper introduces World In-Context Learning, where robot agents encode task steps and object roles semantically rather than visually, enabling manipulation policies to generalize across different scenes without retraining on each world.
ai.why: It shows a path to more adaptable robot controllers that can leverage prior demonstrations in new environments.

title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
excerpt: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. Unlike recent TTS pipelines, WaveGen does not rely on separately trained or externally decoded intermediate representations, such as neural audio codecs, Mel-spectrogram vocoders, or VAE-based latent models. In addition, WaveGen performs internal text-speech alignment within a single model, eliminating the need for external alignment modules such as duration predictors. To preserve a truly end-to-end…

ai.summary: WaveGen is a diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework that generates audio directly from text without relying on intermediate representations like neural audio codecs or Mel-spectrogram vocoders. It jointly learns internal spectral and target waveform trajectories within a single model.
ai.why: Offers a simpler, end-to-end architecture for TTS developers looking to reduce pipeline complexity and latency.

title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
excerpt: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world somewhere, fixing the task, the data, or the timeline, and thereby remove these failures instead of measuring them. We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy sampled from a compositional…

ai.summary: FINCOSMOS proposes an open‑world benchmark for financial language agents that requires live web data, user‑defined strategies, and time‑sensitive evaluation to expose failures like silent mis‑strategies or future‑leak backtests.

title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
excerpt: Few-step sampling reduces the cost of streaming video generation. Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) supervises few-step generators with a separate fake-score network, which adds training memory and computation and must track the evolving generator. We extend APEX to streaming video by using condition shifting to estimate the velocity field of the generated distribution within the generator. The original text condition selects generation, while a shifted condition selects fake estimation using the same parameters. title: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations
excerpt: Weight-activation quantization can reduce the memory and compute cost of neural-network inference, but recent methods often require expensive optimization and architecture-specific propagation of basis transforms across layers. We introduce MACaQ, an MXFP4 W4A4 post-training quantization method that treats every linear layer independently. MACaQ applies a per-channel scale and a block-Hadamard transform online to each layer's activations, while absorbing the corresponding inverse transforms into its weights. ai.summary: The paper introduces MACaQ, a post‑training quantization method that quantizes weights and activations to 4‑bit (W4A4) using per‑channel scaling and a block‑Hadamard transform applied independently to each linear layer.

title: Test-Time Scaling for Diffusion Language Models with Frequency-Aware Remasking
excerpt: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, where decisions about which tokens to commit or remask strongly affect output quality. Existing certainty-aware strategies rely on instantaneous confidence or entropy, but these local signals can be misleading on difficult reasoning problems. We formulate DLM test-time scaling as adaptive allocation of both inference compute and decoding strategies. Our two-stage approach uses a fast base sampler to solve easy questions, then applies frequency-aware remasking to the remaining hard questions. ai.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage test-time scaling method for diffusion language models that uses frequency-aware remasking to adaptively allocate inference compute, improving performance on difficult reasoning tasks compared to standard entropy-based strategies.

title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
excerpt: Scaling depth is a key route to stronger large language models, but Pre-LN architectures often suffer from depth-wise information dilution, limiting the effective use of deep layers. While cross-layer connectivity has proven effective at mitigating this problem, existing designs usually introduce additional computation or memory access. We revisit cross-layer KV sharing as an efficient form of such connectivity. Beyond cache compression, each KV reuse edge creates a direct gradient path from deep layers to source KV projections, turning KV sharing into an implicit structural regularizer for KV representation geometry. We provide a systematic analysis of this mechanism, showing that proper…

ai.summary: DepthGraft introduces hierarchical cross‑layer KV reconstruction, reusing key‑value pairs across transformer layers to create direct gradient paths and mitigate depth‑wise information dilution without extra compute.

title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
excerpt: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same…

ai.summary: The paper shows that memory‑augmented vision‑language‑action policies that store frames uniformly over time fail to distinguish waiting from action, leading to temporal shortcuts.

title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
excerpt: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. excerpt: A scientific agent can give the same verdict while reading and citing different evidence. title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
excerpt: External memory enables LLM agents to improve from experience by distilling trajectories of past tasks into concise lessons for new tasks. However, memory can also lead to memory-induced degradation, where an agent fails on tasks it would solve without memory, often because it follows a lesson that is incorrect, or misapplies or misreads a valid one. This is because lessons are inferred from trajectories labeled only with task success or failure, yet are typically provided without the trajectories they came from, leaving the agent no way to check them.
